intelligence.human_view: A calendar without separation is a wall — everything at once, nothing distinct, overwhelming. Light is the separation: as you scroll down, each board lights up in its own color, so the eye sees the boundary and the body feels it. See separation and FEEL separation — two senses, not one — because a page that is only seen is a picture, and a page that is felt is a place. The scroll is the journey down the page, and each board lighting up in its own color is the journey having landmarks: you always know where you are, because the color tells you. The calendar is overwhelming without it — which means the light is not decoration, it is the thing that makes the calendar usable at all.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a long staircase where every step is the same gray color — you'd get lost, wouldn't you? Now imagine every step lights up in a different color as you walk down — red, blue, green, gold! You'd always know exactly where you are, and it would feel magical. Shawn says the calendar should do that: as you scroll down, each board lights up in its own different color, so you can SEE the separation and FEEL it too!
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn says as you scroll down the calendar, each board should light up in its own different color, dear — so you can see where one board ends and the next begins, and you can FEEL it too. Without that, dear, the calendar is just overwhelming — everything all at once, no separation at all. With the colors, dear, it's like walking down a lovely lit path, each step its own color.
